title: Magnets and Electromagnets
subject: Science
source: NYSED 2024 Grade 5 ELS Released Items, Questions 30-34
directions: Base your answers to questions 30 through 34 on the information below and on your knowledge of science.

intro.html: A student made a simple magnet holder using a clothespin, a plastic cup, a magnet, and tape (Diagram 1). This setup was used to investigate magnetic forces by determining the number of paper clips held by a magnet by direct contact (Diagram 2). Each paper clip was bent to form a hook to attach to other clips hanging below the magnet.

items.caption: Diagram 1
items.alt: Drawing of an upside-down plastic cup sitting on a block. A clothespin is taped to the top of the cup. The clothespin holds a bar magnet that sticks out past the edge of the cup. Labels: Magnet, Clothespin, Plastic cup.

items.caption: Diagram 2
items.alt: The same magnet holder with a chain of four paper clips hanging from the bottom of the magnet. Each paper clip is bent into a hook that holds the clip below it. Label: Paper clip.

tape.html: The student then added different numbers of pieces of tape to the bottom of the magnet and repeated the investigation for each of these different numbers of tape (Diagram 3).

tape.caption: Diagram 3
tape.alt: The same magnet holder. A hand holds a strip of tape under the magnet, and a piece of tape is already stuck to the bottom of the magnet. Label: Tape.

fridge.html: The student is designing a refrigerator magnet to display papers and photographs. Various types of refrigerator magnets are shown in the photograph below.

fridge.alt: Black-and-white photograph of the doors of a stainless steel refrigerator. A photograph, notes, and sheets of notepaper are held on the doors by round magnets and small rectangular magnets. One small note is clipped to another note with a paper clip.

electromagnet.html: An electromagnet is a magnet that is created using electricity. The diagram below is an example of a simple electromagnet — a single wire coiled around a nail. The wire is connected to a battery and has electric current flowing through it.

electromagnet.caption: Simple Electromagnet
electromagnet.alt: Drawing of a battery marked with a plus sign and a minus sign. A wire runs from the top of the battery, wraps around a nail many times, and runs back to the bottom of the battery. Labels: Battery, Coiled wire, Nail.

electromagnet.html: The electric current in the wire causes the electromagnet to act like a regular magnet. Engineers use electromagnets when they design and build motors. Motors are found in everyday objects, such as refrigerators and golf carts.

A student repeats the investigation using an electromagnet. The table below shows how the number of coils around a nail in an electromagnet affects the number of paper clips held when a 4-volt battery is used and when an 8-volt battery is used.

items.stem: Which question is the student investigating?
options: How can the patterns of a magnet’s motion in various situations be observed and measured?
How is the strength of the magnetic force acting on objects affected by the distance between the objects and a magnet?
How does the force of gravity affect the strength of the magnetic force on an object?
How do contact magnetic forces affect the energy transferred between objects?

items.stem: Based on what was learned in the investigations, identify one factor that needs to be considered when designing this refrigerator magnet. [1]
rubric: Allow 1 credit. Acceptable responses include, but are not limited to:
the thickness of paper/object held on refrigerator
the weight/mass of object/paper held on refrigerator

items.stem: A student inspected the data to determine the relationship between the voltage of the battery and magnetic force exerted by the electromagnet. Which question was most likely being investigated?
options: How did changing the number of coils in the electromagnet affect the number of paper clips held by the electromagnet connected to a 4-volt battery?

For the same number of coils around the nail, how did the number of paper clips held by the electromagnet connected to a 4-volt battery compare to the number of paper clips held by the electromagnet connected to an 8-volt battery?
How does keeping the number of coils around the nail constant affect the number of paper clips held by the electromagnet connected to the 8-volt battery?
For an increasing number of coils around the nail, how did the number of paper clips held by the electromagnet change for the electromagnet connected to the 4-volt and 8-volt battery?

items.stem: The student wants to optimize the design of the electromagnet and needs accurate data. How would performing more trials in this investigation improve the reliability of the data collected?
options: More trials produce more data, which is used to reduce human error.
More trials always produce the same data, which can be used to solve a problem.
Averaging data from more trials can help determine which variables are controlled.
Averaging data from more than three trials always increases the error in the data.
